cells.tense: Right now the mind is resting inside its own balance, and that still point is holding while endings come.
cells.act: cross over to the people it actually requires
cells.ask: Name the person this ending actually concerns, and go to them — one honest conversation about what is being closed.
cells.core:
You've found the still point in the middle of a clearing-out. Before anything gets decided or said, the mind settles into its own balance, and from there the endings come one at a time instead of in a rush. That quiet is doing work — you can tell because what you close, you close without flinching.

The clearing isn't over. There's a person on the other side of it you've kept at arm's length, and this connection goes through them or it doesn't go. Go over. One real conversation about what's ending is worth more than a hundred managed silences. What stays afterward is a connection that lived through the ending, which is not the same as one that was spared it.
cells.sheetLine: The mind is still. Let the ones it concerns hear it from you.
cells.verb: settling the mind into balance before anything is closed

cells.tense: The mind keeps rehearsing a future ending it cannot write yet, and the rehearsal is out ahead of the actual clearing.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: When someone pushes you to hurry the closing along, stay on the heading you already chose, once, without renegotiating it.
cells.core:
You're bracing. The mind has gone past the present quiet into a future where everything is already settled, and it keeps writing that ending before the life it belongs to has arrived. The still point is in you somewhere; the bracing has buried it under plans for a close that hasn't come.

What's called for isn't more planning. It's standing on the direction you already chose the next time somebody pushes you to hurry it, or the next time you push yourself. Hold the heading once. You'll know the ending is real when you can sit in it rather than argue with it. Until then, the calm you had is what you're defending, not the timing.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is being rehearsed before it is here.
cells.verb: settling the mind into balance before anything is closed

cells.tense: The mind was at rest back there, and the present clearing is still being stood at from the far side of that door.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Think of one thing this ending makes room for, and let yourself be drawn toward it a little — look at it up close, without committing.
cells.core:
The stillness got left behind. The clearing is happening around you and the mind is standing on the wrong side of it, at a door that already closed. The ability to rest in your own balance is still there; it isn't reaching the present, so the endings feel like they're being done to you rather than by you.

Nothing here needs forcing. What's empty is the pull — the sense that something on the other side is worth walking toward. So look at one of those things without deciding anything. A possibility you can feel from here is enough; the appetite comes back at its own pace. Don't ask the clearing for energy yet. Ask it what it opened.
cells.sheetLine: You are standing past a door that already closed behind you.
cells.verb: settling the mind into balance before anything is closed

cells.tense: The mind is steady and the endings are being made, but the steadying is going unaccounted for as yours.
cells.act: leave the hollow ritual for the living one
cells.ask: At a gathering you attend out of habit rather than want, leave early — and spend that hour with the person or table you would choose.
cells.core:
The calm you bring into endings is real, and you've been treating it as something that happens to you rather than something you do. The clearing goes better because you stay level through it. Nobody outside can see the leveling, so it doesn't get named — and you've stopped naming it too.

Which makes some of the endings look like they're happening without you. They aren't. There's a simpler form of what you keep doing: hold the connection that's alive, and stop feeding the one that's through. When you're somewhere out of routine instead of want, leave early and spend the hour where you'd choose to be. The same quiet, only with you in it.
cells.sheetLine: You steady the endings. That part is not happening to you.
cells.verb: settling the mind into balance before anything is closed

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the mind's quiet here is chosen calibration rather than simple fatigue or avoidance; the record gives a mechanism (Tune through Cognition), not the person's motive. A reader might say 'no, I'm just tired,' and that's fine — the ask is still a workable act whether the quiet is read right or wrong. The sentence serving the writer more than the person is any line implying the endings are already accepted; I've cut that and left the clearing as the place, not the accomplishment.
